ALBERT McCOY AUTO MECHANIC Hunters, Wash. Hunters, Wash., May 10, 1920 Supt of Cushman School Cushman School Tacoma, WA Dear Sir, Enclosed please find check for Leonard's fair. Yours truly, Albert McCoy Cushman Indian School Tacoma, Wash., May 23, 1919 Mr. Albert McCoy Miles, Wash. Dear Sir: Replying to your letter of May 19, 1919: Please sign the enclosed Vacation Request and return same from your son Leonard to this office immediately so that Leonard may accompany the other Colville children home. If the Vacation Request is returned, properly signed, Leonard will be able to leave Cushman on Saturday, June 14, 1919. Very respectfully, Superintendent. /MG Enc. Miles Wash. May 19, 1919 Dept. of Cushman School Ocana Wash Dear Sir, Enclosed find check which I am send you to pay for Leonard McCoy Fair. I wish you would send him home with some of the other children that may come back this way and let me know when. Leaves so that I may meet him at Creston or Davenport. From yours & Ever Respectfully, Albert McLog Miles Wash Please tell Leonard that I have sent the money for him to come home on vacation. Ame Cushman Ind. School, Oct. 1, 1918. Mr. Thompson: The bearer is Leonard McCoy, aged 8, who has just arrived from Miles, Wash., for enrollment. Respectfully, Lucy N. Smith Asst. clerk to take steps to purchase new homes. Two of the families have chosen homes in white farming communities, which will result to their very great advantage. Very respectfully, Superintendent June Comment on Incidents of Importance Names of Deserters During This Month Names of Pupils Granted Leave Cushman Indian School, Tacoma, Wash., Oct. 1, 1918. Mr. Albert McCoy, Miles, Washington, Dear Sir: This is to advise that your son Leonard arrived here safely today. I enclose the application blank which you will please fill out, sign and return. The boy's birth date, name of school he attended, his parent's tribe and degree of Indian blood they possess, should be inserted on the form enclosed. Please state somewhere on the blank which denomination you wish Leonard to attend, Catholic or Protestant. He claims that his mother was Catholic. Awaiting the early return of the application, I am, Yours very truly, Superintendent WESTERN UNION TELEGRAM NEWCOMB CARLTON, PRESIDENT GEORGE W. E. ATKINS, FIRST VICE-PRESIDENT RECEIVED AT 1007 PACIFIC AVE., TACOMA, WASH. ALWAYS OPEN D153EA BM 13 DAVENPORT WASH 530P SEPT 30 1918 SUPT CUSHMAN SCHOOL TACOMA WASH MEET LEONARD MCCOY AT THE GREAT NORTHERN DEPOT ABOUT 2 PM OCTOBER FIRST ALBERT MCCOY FOR FILE Cushman Indian School Tacoma, Wash., May 22, 1919 Albert McCoy Miles, Wash. Dear Sir: Enclosed herewith find Official Receipt No. 131319 for $6.00 for account of Leonard McCoy. Very respectfully, Superintendent. /MG ENC. Tacoma, Wash. Sept. 25, 1918. Mr. Albert McCoy, Miles, Washington. Dear Sir: I have been advised by Mr. Fred Freeman of this school who was recently on the Colville Reservation soliciting pupils, that you have two children Leonard aged 9 and Grace aged 7, whom you desire to enroll in the Cushman School provided Grace is accepted; You are to pay their transportation to the school. I enclose two applications which you will please fill out and return for the enrollment of your children, and I will then forward it to Supt. Upchurch for his endorsement. As the school began two weeks ago, it is advisable to get the children in soon that they may be able to keep up with their classes during the year. Upon arrival at Tacoma, take the "Portland Avenue" car on Pacific Avenue and get off at 32nd street. The school is 4 blocks east from that point. If you are not intending to accompany the children to Cushman, wire me when they start at what time and on what train they arrive in Tacoma that I may meet them. Hoping for an early reply, or the arrival of the children, I am, Yours very truly, Superintendent Albert McCoy Miles, Mo., has two children Grace age 7 and Leonard 9 he will pay their transportation if you will take the girl. [signature] CUSHMAN TRADES SCHOOL Tacoma, Washington. August 16th, 1918. Mr. Albert Mc.Coy, Miles, Wn. Thru the Superintendent Dear Mr. Mc.Coy: Replying to your letter of August 9th 1918. Your application for the enrolment of your two children has been received. Provided Superintendent Upchurch recommends the enrolment of your son, his application will be approved. The girl is only five years old, consequently it is impossible to receive her unless you are able to pay the tuition fee of two hundred dollars a year. Our facilities for the care of babies are very poor. Very sincerely, Superintendent Miles Wash. Aug 9, 1918 Superintendent Cushman School Tacoma, Wash. Dear Sir, I would like to send two of my children to your school—one boy 8 years old and the girl is 5. They have no mother. They are related to the Mosell children. Please let me know at once if you'll take them. I will pay their fare. Address: Albert Mcloy Miles Wash. Cushman Indian School, Tacoma, Wash. Oct. 7, 1918. Mr. Albert McCoy, Miles, Washington. Dear Mr. McCoy: Leonard arrived safely and is in school now. He is well; and if at any time he falls seriously ill, you will be promptly notified. Very sincerely yours, Superintendent Miles Wash. Oct 24, 1918 Super. J Cushman School Tacoma, WA Dear Sirs — will you please let me know weather. Leonard McLoy arrived at your school all O.K. I sent him Sept 30th on the west bound train leaving Davenport Wash at 4:27. I was to arrive at Tacoma Oct 1st about 2 P.M. Answer by return mail Albert McLoy Miles Wash. I wired you a message. 5-1142 DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR UNITED STATES INDIAN SERVICE Spokane Indian Agency, Wellpinit, Wash. May 27, 1919. Mr. E. H. Hammond, Supt., Cushman Indian School, Tacoma, Wash. Dear Mr. Hammond: Vacation request for Leonard McCoy has been forwarded to his father for signature. Respectfully, [signature] Superintendent. OCU/G Cushman Indian School Tacoma, Wash., May 23, 1919 Mr. O. C. Upchurch, Supt. Spokane Indian Agency Wellpinit, Wash. Dear Mr. Upchurch: Enclosed herewith find Vacation Request from Leonard McCoy. If the Request is approved, kindly forward it to Mr. Albert McCoy, Miles, Wash., for signature and return same to this office immediately. The deposit to defray transportation expenses has already been made by Mr. McCoy. Very respectfully, Superintendent. /MG Enc. CASE RECORD. NAME: Leonard McCoy Sex: Male Tribe: Palouse State: Wash. This form must be executed in duplicate when a child is transferred from a reservation to a nonreservation school. The Superintendent of the nonreservation school will retain the original for his files, and the duplicate shall be deposited in the reservation school records. The reservation superintendent should send to the Commissioner of Indian Affairs his certificate as provided by law. All the blanks must be properly filled in every case. If the information called for on any part of the blank is not known, that fact should be stated. No space should be left unfilled. Whether the parents are living or dead, their names must be given. The person who signs the blank as consenting to the transfer should indicate his relation to the applicant by marking out the word "parent," "guardian," or "next of kin," leaving unmarked only the title appropriate to the signer. INDORSEMENTS. The laws relating to the transfer of Indian children from reservations and schools are as follows: That hereafter no Indian child shall be sent from any Indian reservation to a school beyond the State or Territory in which said reservation is situated without the voluntary consent of the father or mother of such child if either of them are living, and if neither of them are living without the voluntary consent of the next of kin of such child. Such consent shall be made before the agent of the reservation, and he shall send to the Commissioner of Indian Affairs his certificate that such consent has been voluntarily given before such child shall be removed from such reservation. And it shall be unlawful for any Indian agent or other employee of the Government to induce, or seek to induce, by withholding rations or by other improper means, the parents or next of kin of any Indian to consent to the removal of any Indian child beyond the limits of any reservation. (28 Stats., p. 906.) Provided, That hereafter no Indian child shall be taken from any school in any State or Territory to a school in any other State against its will or without the written consent of its parents. (29 Stats., p. 348.) That no Indian pupil under the age of fourteen years shall be transported at Government expense to any Indian school beyond the limits of the State or Territory in which the parents of such child reside or of the adjoining State or Territory. (35 Stat. L., 781.) The rules provide that— A pupil who has been regularly enrolled in a nonreservation school must not be taken to any other nonreservation school without the consent of both Superintendents and the Commissioner of Indian Affairs, and superintendents will be held to strict accountability for such pupils taken to their schools. An Indian boy or girl 18 years old and over may, without the consent of parents or others, personally sign the application form on its being changed to suit the case; but in all cases where the parents are living they should first be consulted. This form is to be used only in transfers from reservations or Indian schools to nonreservation schools. RECORD OF PUPIL IN SCHOOL CUSHMAN AGENCY School. TACOMA, WASHINGTON (Location.)
